key_insight: A low-pressure xenon plasma cell can convert deep-UV laser photons into electricity with very high modeled efficiency by combining photoionization with magnetically controlled charge separation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new receiver architecture for space laser power beaming that could avoid many thermal losses typical of semiconductor photovoltaic systems.
method: Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulation of a low-pressure xenon chamber
58.4 nm pulsed laser drives xenon photoionization and plasma formation
Parameter scans over bias voltage, magnetic field, and gas pressure
evidence_signal: The simulations predict 82.25% steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency at 2000 W/m2 average incident power, with energy accounting closing to within 1%.
watch_item: The concept is still simulation-based and depends on tight control of vacuum-ultraviolet absorption, electron confinement, and chamber conditions in a space-compatible implementation.
paper_title: Laser power transmission in space: Plasma-based power cell
